Alex R.: Heads-up: follow-up to the kernel-selection & attn-optimization RFC. We still need to finalize the paged/blocked KV eviction + pinning interface so both streaming-attn and block-attn kernels can run without pathological stalls. Quick thread to land decisions.

Alex R.: Key open questions: 1) soft vs hard pin semantics for in-flight KV spans? 2) eviction priority tie-breaker (age vs last-use vs kernel affinity)? 3) compaction windows / fragmentation thresholds we use for aggressive compaction?

Marta L.: @Alex R. +1. My working proposal: default to soft-pin (prevents immediate paging of a span but allows async eviction under extreme memory pressure). Add explicit hard_pin(span, timeout_ms) for kernels that require contiguous slabs (block-attn). Sketch: 
```
# KV pin API (sketch)
handle = kv.pin(span_id, mode="soft")  # non-blocking, hint to keep resident
handle = kv.pin(span_id, mode="hard", timeout_ms=200)  # block until contiguous allocation or error
kv.unpin(handle)
```
Soft pins are cheap and used by streaming-attn; hard pins reserve contiguous range and are charged to kernel quota.

Raj P.: Soft-pin + hard-pin mix makes sense. Two caveats: (1) fragmentation — hard pins must either reserve contiguous slab slices or fail early; otherwise compaction becomes O(n) and can OOM. (2) compaction scheduling: run low-pri background compactor with exponential backoff; trigger aggressive compaction when free_contiguous_slabs < threshold. For kernel selection heuristics: prefer streaming-attn when avg_seq_len < 512 OR page_hit_rate > 0.7; otherwise block-attn with hard_pin.

Sam T.: If hard_pin fails, what's the behavior? Kernel should be able to fallback without blowing the request. Proposal: fallback policy table per model-version that lists fallback kernels (e.g., block-attn -> streaming-attn, or block-attn-quantized). We should expose a short-circuit policy so caller can opt-in to best-effort vs strict.

Yuki N.: Lab perf numbers to inform thresholds: on 8xA100 testbed, hard_pin adds ~1.2ms per pin call under 80% memory usage but eliminates 20–30% of late scatter page faults for block-attn. Soft-pin + async prefetch gives ~0.5ms avg savings but leaves heavier 95th pctl tails. Will upload traces.

Raj P.: Also add a "pin_hint" field to routing metadata so the scheduler can prefer nodes with contiguous free ranges for a given model. Quota accounting: hard_pin consumes kernel-contiguous_quota so we can deny or queue requests rather than fail silently.

Marta L.: Ops notes: compaction policy defaults: idle_compact_interval = 10s (low priority), aggressive_compact_threshold = free_contiguous_slabs < 5%, fragmentation_ratio_alert = >0.35. Expose metrics: kv.fragmentation_ratio, kv.hard_pin_fail_rate, kv.soft_pin_evictions, kv.contiguous_free_slabs.

Alex R.: Action items: @Marta implement pin API + metrics + default compaction params. @Raj add scheduler pin_hint + quota enforcement. @Yuki run perf regressions on 2-week production trace and post numbers. @Sam define model fallback policy schema and docs. We'll reconvene Wed next week to review telemetry and any regressions. :thumbsup:
